instruction: Display the Properties panel so you can view and edit object properties and formatting settings.

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(5); pyautogui.press('esc'); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.press('f10'); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.press('right', presses=2, interval=0.1); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.press('down', presses=13, interval=0.1); pyautogui.press('enter')

metadata.explanation: This task requires the user to show the Properties panel in LibreOffice Impress. The config hides it using View menu navigation (F10 -> right 2x -> down 13x -> enter). The evaluator checks if 'Properties' is present in the accessibility tree by searching through panel, scroll-pane, filler, or tool-bar elements.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly extracts UI state using accessibility tree to check panel visibility
Metric function properly searches for Properties panel in appropriate element types (panel, scroll-pane, filler, tool-bar)
Expected value handling is correct: uses expected.get('panel_name') which correctly accesses the rules dict for type='rule'
Complete coverage: instruction requires making Properties panel visible, evaluator checks exactly that
Logic is robust with substring matching for panel names and exception handling
No postconfig needed: accessibility tree reflects current UI state after user action
